30	
31	## Access Control
32	
33	### Slot Usage Limiter
34	
35	Decrements an `input_number` helper each time a user's PIN is used. When
36	the counter reaches 0, that user is automatically disabled. Optionally resets
37	the counter when the user is re-enabled.
38	
39	- Set counter to **-1** for unlimited uses
40	- Set counter to **0** to disable on next use
41	- The optional lock filter matches the use's `target` — the lock that
42	  reported it, or whatever `lock_code_manager.use_credential` was told the
43	  credential acted on
44	
45	- **Operations that spend a use** picks which recorded uses count, by what
46	  the device did with the credential: `unlock` and `unknown` by default,
47	  `lock` not
48	- Only a PIN use (`event_type` `pin`) spends a use. Disabling the user takes
49	  away the PIN Lock Code Manager manages, but a card, fingerprint or face
50	  enrolled on the lock itself keeps working, so counting those would spend a
51	  limit that cannot be enforced on them
52	
53	> **Breaking: the entity now records more than unlocks.** It used to record
54	> only unlocks; it records every use of the user's credential now, including
55	> a lock reporting which slot *locked* it and every use reported through
56	> `lock_code_manager.use_credential`. **Operations that spend a use** is what
57	> keeps that from changing your counters: leaving it at its default spends a
58	> use on `unlock` and `unknown` and not on `lock`, so a guest who unlocks
59	> with their PIN and locks up behind them with the same PIN spends one use
60	> rather than two — on a 1-use code, being polite would otherwise lock them
61	> out. Uses reported through `lock_code_manager.use_credential` are always
62	> `unknown`, since Lock Code Manager never actuates a lock and so never sees
63	> what happened next; clear `unknown` and those stop counting entirely. Slot
64	> Usage Notifier has no such filter and runs on every use, locking included;
65	> its `operation` variable says which happened.
66	
67	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fslot_usage_limiter.yaml)
68	
69	| Input | Description | Default |
70	| ----- | ----------- | ------- |
71	| Credential used event entity | The user's event entity, which fires when their credential is used | Required |
72	| Operations that spend a use | Which uses decrement the counter, by what the device did: `unlock`, `lock`, `unknown` | `unlock`, `unknown` |
73	| Locks (optional) | Only count uses whose target is one of these | All targets |
74	| Slot enabled switch | The user's Enabled switch, turned off when the counter runs out | Required |
75	| Uses counter | `input_number` helper tracking remaining uses | Required |
76	| Initial uses on re-enable | Number of uses to reset to when the user is re-enabled (0 = no reset) | 0 |
77	| Notification service (optional) | Service called when the user is disabled | None |
78	
79	### Calendar Condition
80	
81	Creates a template binary sensor that turns ON when a calendar
82	event is active and an optional condition template evaluates to
83	true. Assign the sensor as a user's condition entity to control when
84	their PIN is active.
85	
86	- Filter by event title, description, or location using Jinja2 templates
87	- Supports any HA calendar integration (local, Google, CalDAV, etc.)
88	- Template variables: `message`, `description`, `location`, `start_time`,
89	  `end_time`, `all_day`, `slot_number`, `config_entry_title`, `name_state`
90	
91	> **Breaking: `lock_entity_ids` is gone.** It came from the credential used
92	> event entity, which no longer lists the config entry's locks as its event
93	> types, and nothing else exposes a config entry's locks to a template.
94	> **A condition template that still references it fails quietly.** Home
95	> Assistant treats an undefined template variable as empty rather than as an
96	> error, so the binary sensor stays available, reads `off`, and the PIN never
97	> activates. The one signal is a log line — `Template variable warning:
98	> 'lock_entity_ids' is undefined when rendering ...` — so check the Home
99	> Assistant log after upgrading. Nothing can make that louder: the sensor
100	> cannot tell an undefined variable from a condition that is honestly false.
101	> There is no replacement and nothing worth stubbing it to. The list was
102	> identical for every slot in the config entry, so
103	> `{{ 'lock.front_door' in lock_entity_ids }}` could only ever be constantly
104	> true or constantly false: a condition entity gates a *user* across every
105	> lock in the entry, and never one lock. Delete the reference to fix the
106	> sensor.
107	
108	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Ftemplate%2Flock_code_manager%2Fcalendar_condition.yaml)
109	
110	| Input | Description | Default |
111	| ----- | ----------- | ------- |
112	| Lock Code Manager config entry | Config entry holding the user | Required |
113	| Slot number | The user's slot number (see [Finding a slot number](#finding-a-slot-number)) | Required |
114	| Calendar entity | Calendar to monitor | Required |
115	| Condition template | Jinja2 template to filter events | `{{ true }}` |
116	
117	### Date Range Condition
118	
119	Creates a template binary sensor that turns ON when the current
120	time is between two `input_datetime` helpers. Use for rental-style
121	access windows with specific check-in/check-out times.
122	
123	- Create `input_datetime` helpers first (Settings > Helpers)
124	- Enable both "Date" and "Time" on each helper for date+time ranges
125	- All comparisons done in UTC for timezone safety
126	
127	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Ftemplate%2Flock_code_manager%2Fdate_range_condition.yaml)
128	
129	| Input | Description | Default |
130	| ----- | ----------- | ------- |
131	| Start date/time | `input_datetime` helper for access window start | Required |
132	| End date/time | `input_datetime` helper for access window end | Required |
133	
134	### Calendar PIN Setter
135	
136	Extracts a PIN from calendar event attributes using a Jinja2
137	template and sets it as a user's PIN. Optionally clears the PIN when
138	the event ends. Useful for automated guest access via shared
139	calendars.
140	
141	- Extract PINs from event title, description, or location
142	- Supports optional notifications when PINs are set/cleared
143	
144	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fcalendar_pin_setter.yaml)
145	
146	| Input | Description | Default |
147	| ----- | ----------- | ------- |
148	| Lock Code Manager config entry | Config entry holding the user | Required |
149	| Slot number | The user whose PIN to set (see [Finding a slot number](#finding-a-slot-number)) | Required |
150	| Calendar entity | Calendar to monitor for events | Required |
151	| PIN template | Jinja2 template to extract the PIN from the event | Required |
152	| Clear PIN when event ends | Clear the PIN when the calendar event ends | `true` |
153	| Notification service (optional) | Service called when the PIN is set or cleared | None |
154

156	
157	## Lock Automation
158	
159	### Auto Re-lock
160	
161	Automatically re-locks a lock after it has been unlocked for a
162	configurable amount of time. Supports separate day and night delays
163	based on the sun entity's state (sunrise/sunset).
164	
165	- If the lock is locked before the timer expires, the lock is skipped
166	- Set night delay to 0 to use the same delay for both day and night
167	- Uses `mode: restart` so a new unlock resets the timer
168	
169	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fauto_relock.yaml)
170	
171	| Input | Description | Default |
172	| ----- | ----------- | ------- |
173	| Lock | Lock entity to auto-relock | Required |
174	| Day delay (minutes) | Minutes to wait before re-locking during the day | 5 |
175	| Night delay (minutes) | Minutes to wait at night (0 = use day delay) | 0 |
176	
177	### Lock on Door Close
178	
179	Automatically locks a lock when a door sensor detects the door
180	has closed while the lock is unlocked.
181	
182	- Only locks if the lock is currently unlocked when door closes
183	- Optional delay to allow the door to fully close before locking
184	- Uses `mode: single` to prevent duplicate lock commands
185	
186	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fdoor_lock_on_close.yaml)
187	
188	| Input | Description | Default |
189	| ----- | ----------- | ------- |
190	| Lock | Lock entity to control | Required |
191	| Door sensor | Binary sensor (door class) for open/closed state | Required |
192	| Lock delay (seconds) | Seconds to wait after door closes before locking | 5 |
193

195	
196	## Notifications
197	
198	### Slot Usage Notifier
199	
200	Runs actions when a user's credential is used on a lock. Use it to
201	send notifications, trigger scripts, or run any HA action.
202	
203	- Template variables: `slot_name`, `slot_num`, `lock_name`, `timestamp`,
204	  `operation`, `credential_type`
205	- `lock_name` and the optional lock filter both read the use's `target` —
206	  the lock that reported it, or whatever `lock_code_manager.use_credential`
207	  was told the credential acted on
208	- Uses `mode: queued` to handle rapid successive uses
209	- **Breaking:** it now runs on every recorded use, locking by code
210	  included, where it used to run only on unlocks. `operation` says which
211	  happened; put it in your message, or skip a kind with a condition inside
212	  your actions
213	
214	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fslot_usage_notifier.yaml)
215	
216	| Input | Description | Default |
217	| ----- | ----------- | ------- |
218	| Credential used event entities | One or more users' event entities | Required |
219	| Locks (optional) | Only run for uses whose target is one of these | All targets |
220	| Actions | HA actions to run (notifications, scripts, etc.) | Required |
221	
222	### Credential Used
223	
224	Runs actions every time a credential is used, whether Lock Code
225	Manager saw it happen on a lock or was told about it through the
226	`lock_code_manager.use_credential` action.
227	
228	- Template variables: `name`, `source`, `target`, `credential_type`,
229	  `operation`, `config_entry_id`, `config_entry_title`, `timestamp`
230	- Every filter is optional; leave them all empty to act on every use
231	- Uses `mode: queued` to handle rapid successive uses
232	
233	Slot Usage Notifier and Slot Usage Limiter trigger on one user's
234	credential used *entity*, so each automation covers the users you point
235	it at. This blueprint triggers on the `lock_code_manager_credential_used`
236	event instead, so one automation covers every user in every
237	configuration, and its filters narrow from there. All three see the same
238	uses: whether Lock Code Manager watched a lock report one or was told
239	about it through `lock_code_manager.use_credential`, and whatever the
240	use was against.
241	
242	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fcredential_used.yaml)
243	
244	| Input | Description | Default |
245	| ----- | ----------- | ------- |
246	| Lock Code Manager config entry (optional) | Only run for uses in this configuration | All configurations |
247	| Users (optional) | Only run for these users, by name | All users |
248	| Sources (optional) | Only run for credentials entered on these entities | Any source |
249	| Targets (optional) | Only run for credentials used against these entities | Any target |
250	| Actions | HA actions to run (notifications, scripts, etc.) | Required |
251

254	## Setup Helpers
255	
256	### Condition Linker
257	
258	A one-shot automation that assigns a condition entity to a user via
259	the `lock_code_manager.set_condition` service. Run it once from
260	the Automations page, then delete or keep for reference.
261	
262	- Uses a synthetic event trigger that never fires automatically
263	- Manually run from the Automations page (three-dot menu > Run)
264	
265	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fcondition_linker.yaml)
266	
267	| Input | Description | Default |
268	| ----- | ----------- | ------- |
269	| Lock Code Manager config entry | Config entry holding the user | Required |
270	| Name | The person to assign the condition to, exactly as they are named in the config entry | Required |
271	| Condition entity | Entity to use as the condition | Required |
272	
273	---
274	
275	## Finding a slot number
276	
277	Lock Code Manager assigns each user a slot number and manages it for
278	you, so the configuration editor and the dashboard cards never show
279	it. Blueprints and services still take one, because a lock addresses
280	its credentials by position.
281	
282	To find the number for a user, open any of that user's entities and
283	look at its `code_slot` attribute. In a template:
284	
285	```jinja
286	{{ state_attr('text.raman_pin', 'code_slot') }}
287	```
288	
289	---
290	
291	## Credential used entity attributes
292	
293	Every user has a `credential_used` event entity. Its state is the
294	timestamp of their last recorded use, and its attributes are what a
295	template or blueprint reads about that use:
296	
297	| Attribute | Meaning |
298	| --------- | ------- |
299	| `event_type` | The kind of credential presented — `pin`, or on a lock that reports which: `rfid` (Matter, ZHA, Zigbee2MQTT), `fingerprint` (Matter, and Zigbee2MQTT when the lock's converter names it) or `face` (Matter). It says *what* was used, never where. On a Zigbee or Z-Wave lock a use is a `pin` only when typed at the keypad or sent with the user's code; the thumb-turn, a remote command naming no user and a source the lock does not identify record no use |
300	| `event_types` | The kinds this user's uses can be: `pin`, plus every kind the configuration's locks can report. A use of a kind not listed here is not recorded on the entity, though `lock_code_manager_credential_used` still fires for it |
301	| `name` | The user whose credential was used |
302	| `target` | What the credential was used against — a lock that reported the use, or whatever `lock_code_manager.use_credential` was told it acted on |
303	| `source` | Where the credential was entered. Same entity as `target` when a lock observed the use itself |
304	| `credential_type` | The kind of credential presented, the same value as `event_type` |
305	| `operation` | What the device did with it: `unlock`, `lock`, or `unknown` when nothing reported which. Always `unknown` for a use reported through `lock_code_manager.use_credential` |
306	| `config_entry_id` | The Lock Code Manager configuration holding the user |
307	| `config_entry_title` | That configuration's title |
308	| `code_slot` | The user's slot number |
309	| `slot_field` | Always `credential_used` |
310	
311	Filtering by credential kind is a template away: `event_type` (or
312	`credential_type`) is `pin` for a PIN and `rfid` for a card read at a lock's
313	own reader, so an automation can act on one kind without acting on every
314	other. The Slot Usage Limiter counts only `pin` uses, since disabling a user
315	cannot stop a card or fingerprint enrolled on the lock itself.
316	
317	> **Breaking:** the entity used to record only unlocks; it now records every
318	> use of the user's credential, including a lock reporting which slot locked
319	> it, and says which in `operation`. Its `event_type` used to be the lock
320	> entity ID and is now the credential kind, so `event_types` is the kinds of
321	> credential rather than a list of locks. It also used to publish the older
322	> lock-shaped payload. Templates reading
323	> `event_type` as a lock must read `target` instead, and
324	> `lock_code_manager_config_entry_id`, `code_slot_name`, `action_text`,
325	> `notification_source`, `from`, `to`, `state`, `entity_id`, `device_id`,
326	> `extra_data` and `lock_config_entry_id` are gone from the entity, and gone
327	> entirely: the `lock_code_manager_lock_state_changed` bus event that used to
328	> carry them was removed in 6.0. What survives of them is on
329	> `lock_code_manager_credential_used` — `target` for the lock, `name` for the
330	> person, `operation` for what the lock did — and the target entity's own state
331	> for the rest.
332

1	# Blueprints
2	
3	> **The Condition Linker takes a name in 6.0.** It used to take a slot number,
4	> and it called an action that 6.0 removed. An automation already created from
5	> it has to be reconfigured with the person's **Name** — or simply recreated,
6	> since it is a one-shot. See [[Upgrading to 6.0|Upgrading-to-6.0]].
7	
8	> **Entity IDs changed in 5.0.** Blueprints take entity IDs as inputs, and
9	> every Lock Code Manager entity was renamed from its slot number onto its
10	> user's name when you upgraded — `..._code_slot_1_pin` became
11	> `..._raman_pin`. Home Assistant does not rewrite IDs stored inside an
12	> automation, so **automations built from these blueprints before 5.0 need
13	> their inputs repointed.** The upgrade leaves a notification listing every
14	> rename. See [[Upgrading to 5.0|Upgrading-to-5.0]].
15	
16	Lock Code Manager provides Home Assistant blueprints for advanced automation use cases. These blueprints let you build custom workflows on top of LCM without modifying the integration itself.
17	
18	Import them using the buttons below, or copy the YAML files from the [`blueprints/`](https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/tree/main/blueprints) directory in the repository.
19	
20	## Slot Usage Limiter
21	
22	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fslot_usage_limiter.yaml)
23	
24	**Type:** Automation
25	
26	Decrements an `input_number` helper each time a user's credential is used. When the counter reaches 0, the user is automatically disabled. Optionally resets the counter when the user is enabled again.
27	
28	### Setup
29	
30	1. Create an `input_number` helper (Settings → Devices & Services → Helpers) with min=0, max=your desired limit, and step=1.
31	2. Import this blueprint using the button above.
32	3. Create a new automation from the blueprint and pick the user's *credential used* event entity, their *enabled* switch, and the helper you created.
33	
34	### Inputs
35	
36	| Input | Description | Default |
37	|-------|-------------|---------|
38	| **Credential used event entity** | The user's `credential_used` event entity. | *(required)* |
39	| **Slot enabled switch** | The user's `enabled` switch, turned off when the counter hits 0. | *(required)* |
40	| **Uses counter** | An `input_number` helper that tracks remaining uses. | *(required)* |
41	| **Operations that spend a use** | Which uses decrement the counter, by what the device did — `unlock`, `lock`, `unknown`. | `unlock`, `unknown` |
42	| **Locks (optional)** | Restrict to a specific lock or set of locks. Empty counts every use. | *(all)* |
43	| **Initial uses on re-enable** | When > 0, the counter resets to this value each time the user is enabled again. Set to 0 to disable auto-reset. | `0` |
44	| **Notification service (optional)** | A notify entity messaged when uses are exhausted and the user is disabled. | *(none)* |
45	
46	> **Why `lock` is off by default.** Since 5.3.0 a credential that *locks* a door
47	> is recorded too. A guest who unlocks with their PIN and locks up behind them
48	> with the same PIN would otherwise spend two uses — locking themselves out of a
49	> one-use code for being polite. Uses reported through
50	> `lock_code_manager.use_credential` are always `unknown`, since nothing told
51	> Lock Code Manager what happened next.
52	
53	> **Note:** This blueprint replaces the built-in *Number of Uses* feature (removed in 2.0) with an `input_number`-based approach. It provides external visibility into the remaining count and allows programmatic reset via automations or the UI.
54	
55	---
56	
57	## Calendar Condition
58	
59	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Ftemplate%2Flock_code_manager%2Fcalendar_condition.yaml)
60	
61	**Type:** Template (binary sensor)
62	
63	Creates a binary sensor that turns ON when a calendar event is active and an optional condition template is truthy. Assign the resulting binary sensor as the [[condition entity|Using-Condition-Entities]] for a Lock Code Manager user.
64	
65	### Setup
66	
67	1. Import this blueprint using the button above.
68	2. Configure it with your LCM config entry, slot number, calendar entity, and optionally a condition template.
69	3. The blueprint creates a binary sensor — assign it as that user's condition entity.
70	
71	### Inputs
72	
73	| Input | Description | Default |
74	|-------|-------------|---------|
75	| **Lock Code Manager config entry** | The LCM config entry that manages your lock(s). | *(required)* |
76	| **Slot number** | The code slot number. Can be a static number or a Jinja2 template using calendar event attributes. | *(required)* |
77	| **Calendar entity** | The calendar entity whose events control this condition. | *(required)* |
78	| **Condition template** | A Jinja2 template that must evaluate to truthy for the sensor to turn ON (in addition to the calendar being active). | `{{ true }}` |
79	
80	### Available Template Variables
81	
82	Your condition template can use these variables:
83	
84	| Variable | Description |
85	|----------|-------------|
86	| `message` | Calendar event summary/title |
87	| `description` | Calendar event description |
88	| `location` | Calendar event location |
89	| `start_time` | Event start time |
90	| `end_time` | Event end time |
91	| `all_day` | Whether the event is an all-day event |
92	| `slot_number` | The resolved slot number |
93	| `config_entry_title` | The LCM config entry title |
94	| `name_state` | The current name of the code slot |
95	
96	### Example Condition Templates
97	
98	- Allow when event title contains "Guest": `{{ 'Guest' in message }}`
99	- Allow only during business hours: `{{ 8 <= now().hour < 18 }}`
100	
101	> **`lock_entity_ids` was removed in 5.3.0 — check your logs after upgrading.**
102	>
103	> A condition template still referencing it **fails quietly**: Home Assistant
104	> treats an undefined variable as empty rather than an error, so the binary
105	> sensor stays available, reads `off`, and **the PIN never activates**. The only
106	> signal is a log line — `Template variable warning: 'lock_entity_ids' is
107	> undefined when rendering ...`. Nothing else will tell you. Remove the
108	> reference to fix the sensor.
109	>
110	> There is no replacement, and it was not worth keeping: the list was the same
111	> for every slot in the config entry, so `{{ 'lock.front_door' in lock_entity_ids }}`
112	> could only ever be constantly true or constantly false. A condition entity
113	> gates a *user* across every lock in the entry; it cannot gate one lock.
114	
115	> **Note:** The condition template and calendar attributes are evaluated when the sensor is first loaded and when Home Assistant reloads template entities. For the default `{{ true }}`, the sensor dynamically tracks the calendar on/off state. For conditions that reference event attributes, reload template entities after calendar event changes to re-evaluate.
116	
117	---
118	
119	## Date Range Condition
120	
121	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Ftemplate%2Flock_code_manager%2Fdate_range_condition.yaml)
122	
123	**Type:** Template (binary sensor)
124	
125	Creates a binary sensor that turns ON when the current time is between two `input_datetime` helper entities. Assign the resulting binary sensor as the [[condition entity|Using-Condition-Entities]] for a Lock Code Manager user.
126	
127	### Setup
128	
129	1. Create two `input_datetime` helpers (Settings → Devices & Services → Helpers) — one for the start date/time and one for the end date/time. Enable both "Date" and "Time" on each helper.
130	2. Import this blueprint using the button above.
131	3. Configure it with your start and end date/time helpers.
132	4. The blueprint creates a binary sensor — assign it as that user's condition entity.
133	
134	### Inputs
135	
136	| Input | Description | Default |
137	|-------|-------------|---------|
138	| **Start date/time** | An `input_datetime` helper that defines when the access window begins. | *(required)* |
139	| **End date/time** | An `input_datetime` helper that defines when the access window ends. | *(required)* |
140	
141	### Example Usage
142	
143	Give a guest temporary access for a specific date range:
144	
145	1. Create `input_datetime.guest_start` and `input_datetime.guest_end` helpers.
146	2. Set the start to your guest's arrival date/time and end to their departure.
147	3. Import this blueprint and select both helpers.
148	4. Assign the resulting binary sensor as the guest's condition entity.
149	
150	> **Tip:** You can display the `input_datetime` helpers inline in the LCM dashboard using the `condition_helpers` configuration property. See [[Using Condition Entities|Using-Condition-Entities#displaying-condition-helper-controls-inline]] for details.
151	
152	---
153	
154	## Condition Linker
155	
156	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fcondition_linker.yaml)
157	
158	**Type:** Automation (one-shot)
159	
160	Calls `lock_code_manager.set_condition` to wire a condition entity to one person. This provides a UI-friendly way to assign condition entities without editing YAML.
161	
162	### Setup
163	
164	1. Import this blueprint using the button above.
165	2. Create a new automation from the blueprint and configure it with your LCM config entry, the person's name, and the condition entity you want to assign.
166	3. Manually run the automation once from the Automations page (three-dot menu → Run).
167	4. The condition entity is now assigned to that person. You can delete the automation afterward or keep it for reference.
168	
169	### Inputs
170	
171	| Input | Description | Default |
172	|-------|-------------|---------|
173	| **Lock Code Manager config entry** | The LCM config entry that manages your lock(s). | *(required)* |
174	| **Name** | The name of the person to assign the condition entity to, as it appears in Lock Code Manager. Matched ignoring case and surrounding spaces. | *(required)* |
175	| **Condition entity** | The entity to use as the condition. Supports `binary_sensor`, `calendar`, `input_boolean`, `schedule`, and `switch` domains. | *(required)* |
176	
177	> **Note:** This automation uses a synthetic event trigger that never fires on its own. You must manually run it from the UI.
178	
179	---
180	
181	## Calendar PIN Setter
182	
183	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fcalendar_pin_setter.yaml)
184	
185	**Type:** Automation
186	
187	Extracts a PIN from calendar event attributes using a user-provided template and sets it on a Lock Code Manager code slot. Optionally clears the PIN when the calendar event ends.
188	
189	### Setup
190	
191	1. Import this blueprint using the button above.
192	2. Create a new automation from the blueprint and configure it with your LCM config entry, calendar entity, slot number, and a PIN template.
193	3. When a calendar event starts, the PIN is extracted and set on the slot. When it ends (if enabled), the PIN is cleared.
194	
195	### Inputs
196	
197	| Input | Description | Default |
198	|-------|-------------|---------|
199	| **Lock Code Manager config entry** | The LCM config entry that manages your lock(s). | *(required)* |
200	| **Slot number** | The code slot number. Can be a static number or a Jinja2 template using calendar event attributes. | *(required)* |
201	| **Calendar entity** | The calendar entity whose events provide PIN codes. | *(required)* |
202	| **PIN template** | A Jinja2 template that extracts a PIN from calendar event attributes. Must evaluate to a non-empty string. | *(required)* |
203	| **Clear PIN when event ends** | When enabled, the PIN is cleared when the calendar event ends. | `true` |
204	| **Notification service (optional)** | A notify entity messaged when PINs are set or cleared. | *(none)* |
205	
206	### Available Template Variables
207	
208	Your PIN and slot number templates can use these variables:
209	
210	| Variable | Description |
211	|----------|-------------|
212	| `message` | Calendar event summary/title |
213	| `description` | Calendar event description |
214	| `location` | Calendar event location |
215	| `start_time` | Event start time |
216	| `end_time` | Event end time |
217	| `all_day` | Whether the event is an all-day event |
218	
219	### Example PIN Templates
220	
221	- Extract a 4-digit PIN from description: `{{ description | regex_findall('\b\d{4}\b') | first | default('') }}`
222	- Use the first 4 characters of the event title: `{{ message[:4] if message | length >= 4 else '' }}`
223	
224	---
225	
226	## Finding a slot number
227	
228	The [Calendar Condition](#calendar-condition) and [Calendar PIN
229	Setter](#calendar-pin-setter) blueprints ask for a **slot number**, and nothing
230	in the user interface shows you one — Lock Code Manager assigns each user a
231	slot and manages it for you, so the configuration dialogs and the dashboard
232	cards deliberately never mention it. Those two still take one because the
233	number can come from a template over the calendar event. Every action, and
234	every other blueprint, addresses the person instead.
235	
236	To find the number for a user, open any of that user's entities and look at
237	its `code_slot` attribute. In a template:
238	
239	```jinja
240	{{ state_attr('text.all_locks_raman_pin', 'code_slot') }}
241	```
242	
243	The number is stable: renaming a user does not change it, which is why
244	renaming is free. It only changes if you remove the user and add them again.
245	
246	---
247	
248	## Combining Blueprints and Condition Logic
249	
250	These blueprints can be combined with each other and with Home Assistant's built-in features for more advanced workflows. Each blueprint controls a different aspect of the same slot independently.
251	
252	### Example: Calendar access with usage limit
253	
254	Give a cleaning crew a code that's only active during scheduled times and expires after a set number of uses:
255	
256	1. **Calendar Condition** — Create a binary sensor from your cleaning schedule calendar. Assign it as the condition entity of the *Cleaners* user (slot 3 in the blueprint). The code is only active during scheduled cleaning events.
257	2. **Slot Usage Limiter** — Set up a usage counter for *Cleaners* with a limit of 5 uses and auto-reset on re-enable.
258	
259	How it works:
260	- When a cleaning event starts, the calendar condition turns ON → LCM activates the code on the lock
261	- Each time the code is used, the usage limiter decrements the counter
262	- If the crew uses the code 5 times, *Cleaners* is disabled (even during an active event)
263	- When the event ends, the calendar condition turns OFF → LCM clears the code
264	- Next event: *Cleaners* is enabled again → counter resets to 5
265	
266	### Example: Dynamic guest codes from a booking calendar
267	
268	Combine all three blueprints for a fully automated guest access system:
269	
270	1. **Calendar Condition** for the *Guest* user (slot 3) → code only active during the booking
271	2. **Calendar PIN Setter** for *Guest* (slot 3) → PIN extracted from the booking description (e.g. "Check-in code: 5678")
272	3. **Slot Usage Limiter** for *Guest* → max 10 uses during the stay
273	
274	### Combining conditions with groups
275	
276	LCM's condition entity accepts any `binary_sensor`. Use Home Assistant's [Group](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/group/) integration to combine multiple conditions into one:
277	
278	- Create a **group** of binary sensors (e.g. calendar condition + presence sensor)
279	- The group turns ON when **all** members are ON (default) or **any** member is ON
280	- Assign the group entity as the user's condition entity
281	
282	**Example:** Code active only during a calendar event AND when the home is in "away" mode:
283	1. Calendar Condition → `binary_sensor.guest_calendar_active`
284	2. Template sensor → `binary_sensor.home_is_away` (based on alarm state)
285	3. Group → `binary_sensor.guest_access_conditions` (all must be ON)
286	4. Assign the group as the user's condition entity
287	
288	### Using templates for custom logic
289	
290	For logic that doesn't fit neatly into blueprints or groups, create a [Template binary sensor](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/template/) and assign it as the condition entity:
291	
292	```yaml
293	template:
294	  - binary_sensor:
295	      - name: "Slot 3 Active"
296	        state: >
297	          {{ is_state('calendar.guest_bookings', 'on')
298	             and states('input_number.guest_uses') | int > 0
299	             and is_state('alarm_control_panel.home', 'armed_away') }}
300	```
301	
302	This gives full Jinja2 flexibility for combining any Home Assistant states into a single condition.
303	
304	---
305	
306	## Auto Re-lock
307	
308	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fauto_relock.yaml)
309	
310	**Type:** Automation
311	
312	Automatically re-locks a lock after it has been unlocked for a configurable amount of time. Supports separate day and night delays based on the sun entity's state (sunrise/sunset).
313	
314	### Setup
315	
316	1. Import this blueprint using the button above.
317	2. Select the lock entity to auto-relock.
318	3. Set the day delay (in minutes). Default: 5 minutes.
319	4. Optionally set a night delay. Set to 0 to use the day delay for both day and night.
320	
321	### Inputs
322	
323	| Input | Description | Default |
324	|-------|-------------|---------|
325	| **Lock** | The lock entity to auto-relock. | *(required)* |
326	| **Day delay (minutes)** | How long to wait before auto-relocking during the day. | `5` |
327	| **Night delay (minutes)** | How long to wait at night (between sunset and sunrise). Set to 0 to use the day delay for both. | `0` |
328	
329	> **Note:** Uses `mode: restart` — if the lock is unlocked again while the timer is running, the timer resets. If the lock is locked before the timer expires, the lock command is skipped.
330	
331	> **Note:** Night detection uses the `sun.sun` entity (Home Assistant Sun integration). If the Sun integration is not enabled, the night delay will never apply.
332	
333	---
334	
335	## Lock on Door Close
336	
337	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fdoor_lock_on_close.yaml)
338	
339	**Type:** Automation
340	
341	Automatically locks a lock when a door sensor detects the door has closed while the lock is unlocked. Useful for ensuring the door is always locked when closed.
342	
343	### Setup
344	
345	1. Import this blueprint using the button above.
346	2. Select the lock entity to control.
347	3. Select the door sensor (binary_sensor with door device class).
348	4. Optionally set a delay before locking. Default: 5 seconds.
349	
350	### Inputs
351	
352	| Input | Description | Default |
353	|-------|-------------|---------|
354	| **Lock** | The lock entity to control. | *(required)* |
355	| **Door sensor** | A binary sensor that detects open/closed state (on = open, off = closed). | *(required)* |
356	| **Lock delay (seconds)** | How long to wait after the door closes before locking. Set to 0 to lock immediately. | `5` |
357	
358	> **Note:** Uses `mode: single` to prevent duplicate lock commands. Only locks if the lock is currently unlocked when the door closes.
359	
360	---
361	
362	## Credential Used
363	
364	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fcredential_used.yaml)
365	
366	**Type:** Automation
367	
368	Runs one or more actions every time a credential is used — whether Lock Code Manager saw a lock report it, or was told through `lock_code_manager.use_credential`.
369	
370	### Which of the three should I use?
371	
372	All three see the same uses. The difference is what they trigger on:
373	
374	- **Slot Usage Notifier** and **Slot Usage Limiter** trigger on one user's `credential_used` *entity*, so each automation covers the users you point it at. Reach for these when you want the focused, per-user recipe.
375	- **Credential Used** triggers on the `lock_code_manager_credential_used` *event*, so one automation covers every user in every configuration, and its filters narrow from there. Reach for this when you want the whole picture.
376	
377	### Inputs
378	
379	| Input | Description | Default |
380	|-------|-------------|---------|
381	| **Actions** | HA actions to run when a credential is used. | *(required)* |
382	| **Lock Code Manager config entry (optional)** | Only act on uses from this configuration. | *(all)* |
383	| **Users (optional)** | Only act on these users, by name. | *(all)* |
384	| **Sources (optional)** | Only act on uses entered at these entities. | *(all)* |
385	| **Targets (optional)** | Only act on uses against these entities. | *(all)* |
386	
387	### Available Template Variables
388	
389	| Variable | Description |
390	|----------|-------------|
391	| `name` | The user whose credential was used |
392	| `source` | The entity ID where the credential was entered |
393	| `target` | The entity ID it was used against |
394	| `credential_type` | The kind of credential presented, e.g. `pin` |
395	| `operation` | What the device did with it: `unlock`, `lock`, or `unknown` |
396	| `config_entry_id` | The ID of the Lock Code Manager configuration |
397	| `config_entry_title` | The title of that configuration |
398	| `timestamp` | Date and time the event occurred (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) |
399	
400	This is the blueprint to use for an external keypad opening something Lock Code Manager doesn't manage — a cover, a relay, an alarm panel. See [[External Keypads|External-Keypads]].
401	
402	---
403	
404	## Slot Usage Notifier
405	
406	[![Import Blueprint](https://my.home-assistant.io/badges/blueprint_import.svg)](https://my.home-assistant.io/redirect/blueprint_import/?blueprint_url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Framan325%2Flock_code_manager%2Fblob%2Fmain%2Fblueprints%2Fautomation%2Flock_code_manager%2Fslot_usage_notifier.yaml)
407	
408	**Type:** Automation
409	
410	Runs actions when a user's credential is used on a lock. Use it to send notifications, trigger scripts, or run any HA action. Uses the HA action selector for full flexibility.
411	
412	### Setup
413	
414	1. Import this blueprint using the button above.
415	2. Select the *credential used* event entity of each user to watch (e.g., "Raman Credential used").
416	3. Configure the actions to run when the PIN is used (notifications, scripts, etc.).
417	
418	### Inputs
419	
420	| Input | Description | Default |
421	|-------|-------------|---------|
422	| **Credential used event entities** | One or more users' `credential_used` event entities. | *(required)* |
423	| **Locks (optional)** | Restrict to a specific lock or set of locks. Empty runs for any lock the event entity reports. | *(all)* |
424	| **Actions** | HA actions to run when a credential is used (notifications, scripts, etc.). | *(required)* |
425	
426	### Available Template Variables
427	
428	Your actions can reference these variables in templates:
429	
430	| Variable | Description |
431	|----------|-------------|
432	| `slot_name` | The name of the user whose credential was used |
433	| `slot_num` | The user's slot number |
434	| `lock_name` | Friendly name of the lock where the credential was used |
435	| `timestamp` | Date and time the event occurred (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) |
436	| `operation` | What the device did with the credential: `unlock`, `lock`, or `unknown` |
437	| `credential_type` | The kind of credential presented, e.g. `pin` |
438	
439	> **Note:** Requires a lock that reports credential use (produces `*_credential_used` events; `*_code_slot_*_pin_used` before 5.0). Uses `mode: queued` with max 10 to handle rapid successive uses.

   132	      selector:

     3	  name: "Lock Code Manager: Calendar Condition"
     4	  description: >
     5	    Creates a binary sensor that turns ON when a calendar event is active and
     6	    an optional condition template is truthy. Assign the resulting binary sensor
     7	    as the condition entity for a Lock Code Manager code slot.
     8	
     9	
    10	    **Available template variables**
    11	
    12	    Your condition template can use these variables:
    13	
    14	    - `message` — calendar event summary/title
    15	
    16	    - `description` — calendar event description
    17	
    18	    - `location` — calendar event location
    19	
    20	    - `start_time` — event start time
    21	
    22	    - `end_time` — event end time
    23	
    24	    - `all_day` — whether the event is an all-day event
    25	
    26	    - `slot_number` — the resolved slot number
    27	
    28	    - `config_entry_title` — the LCM config entry title
    29	
    30	    - `name_state` — the current name of the code slot
    31	
    32	
    33	    **Removed: `lock_entity_ids`**
    34	
    35	
    36	    This variable no longer exists. It was read off the credential used event
    37	    entity, which used to list the config entry's lock entity IDs as its event
    38	    types and now records one fixed event type instead. Nothing else in Home
    39	    Assistant exposes a config entry's locks to a template, so there is no
    40	    replacement.
    41	
    42	
    43	    A condition template that still references it fails quietly. Home
    44	    Assistant treats an undefined template variable as empty rather than as
    45	    an error, so the binary sensor stays available, reads `off`, and the PIN
    46	    never activates. The one signal is a line in the Home Assistant log:
    47	    `Template variable warning: 'lock_entity_ids' is undefined when rendering
    48	    ...`. Check the log after upgrading — nothing else will tell you.
    49	
    50	
    51	    Nothing here can make that louder, and there is nothing worth stubbing
    52	    the variable to: the sensor cannot tell an undefined variable from a
    53	    condition that is honestly false. Nor was the variable worth keeping. The
    54	    list was the same for every slot in the config entry, so
    55	    `{{ 'lock.front_door' in lock_entity_ids }}` could only ever be constantly
    56	    true or constantly false. A Lock Code Manager condition entity gates a
    57	    *user* across every lock in the entry; it cannot gate one lock. Remove the
    58	    reference to fix the sensor.
    59	
    60	
    61	    **Example condition templates**

    63	    - Allow when event title contains "Guest": `{{ 'Guest' in message }}`

     2	blueprint:
     3	  name: "Lock Code Manager: Date Range Condition"
     4	  description: >
     5	    Creates a binary sensor that turns ON when the current time is between
     6	    two `input_datetime` helper entities. Assign the resulting binary sensor
     7	    as the condition entity for a Lock Code Manager code slot.
     8	
     9	
    10	    **Setup**
    11	
    12	    1. Create two `input_datetime` helpers (Settings -> Devices & Services ->
    13	       Helpers) — one for the start date/time and one for the end date/time.
    14	       Enable both "Date" and "Time" on each helper.
    15	
    16	    2. Import this blueprint and configure it with your start and end
    17	       date/time helpers.
    18	
    19	    3. The blueprint creates a binary sensor — assign it as the condition
    20	       entity for your code slot.
    21	
    22	
    23	    **How it works**
    24	
    25	    The sensor is ON when `now()` is between the start and end date/times.
    26	    If either helper is `unknown` or `unavailable`, the sensor becomes
    27	    unavailable (condition blocks access).
    28	  domain: template
    29	  # yamllint disable-line rule:line-length
    30	  source_url: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/blob/main/blueprints/template/lock_code_manager/date_range_condition.yaml
    31	  input:
    32	    start_datetime:
    33	      name: Start date/time
    34	      description: >
    35	        An `input_datetime` helper that defines when the access window
    36	        begins.
    37	      selector:
    38	        entity:
    39	          domain: input_datetime
    40	    end_datetime:
    41	      name: End date/time
    42	      description: >
    43	        An `input_datetime` helper that defines when the access window
    44	        ends.
    45	      selector:
    46	        entity:
    47	          domain: input_datetime
    48	
    49	variables:
    50	  start_entity: !input start_datetime
    51	  end_entity: !input end_datetime
    52	
    53	binary_sensor:
    54	  - state: >-
    55	      {% set start = states(start_entity) %}
    56	      {% set end = states(end_entity) %}
    57	      {% if start in ['unknown', 'unavailable'] or end in ['unknown', 'unavailable'] %}
    58	        false
    59	      {% else %}
    60	        {% set start_dt = start | as_datetime | as_utc %}
    61	        {% set end_dt = end | as_datetime | as_utc %}
    62	        {{ start_dt <= utcnow() <= end_dt }}
    63	      {% endif %}
    64	    availability: >-
    65	      {% set start = states(start_entity) %}
    66	      {% set end = states(end_entity) %}
    67	      {{ start not in ['unknown', 'unavailable'] and end not in ['unknown', 'unavailable'] }}

     2	blueprint:
     3	  name: "Lock Code Manager: Auto Re-lock"
     4	  description: >
     5	    Automatically re-locks a lock after it has been unlocked for a
     6	    configurable amount of time. Supports separate day and night delays
     7	    based on the sun entity's state.
     8	
     9	
    10	    **How it works**
    11	
    12	    When the lock is unlocked, a timer starts. If the lock is not manually
    13	    locked before the timer expires, the automation locks it automatically.
    14	    If the lock is locked before the timer expires (manually or by another
    15	    automation), the timer is cancelled.
    16	
    17	
    18	    **Day/night support**
    19	
    20	    Optionally configure a shorter delay for nighttime (between sunset and
    21	    sunrise). If night delay is set to 0, the day delay is used for both
    22	    day and night.
    23	
    24	
    25	    **Setup**
    26	
    27	    1. Import this blueprint and create an automation from it.
    28	
    29	    2. Select the lock entity to auto-relock.
    30	
    31	    3. Set the day delay (in minutes). Default: 5 minutes.
    32	
    33	    4. Optionally set a night delay (in minutes). Set to 0 to use the day
    34	       delay for both. Default: 0 (disabled).
    35

    39

    46

    52	
    53	    **Setup**
    54	
    55	    1. Import this blueprint and create an automation from it.
    56

    59	    3. Configure the actions to run when a credential is used.
    60	  domain: automation

    62	  source_url: https://github.com/raman325/lock_code_manager/blob/main/blueprints/automation/lock_code_manager/slot_usage_notifier.yaml

    73	          integration: lock_code_manager
    74	          multiple: true
    75	    locks:
    76	      name: Locks (optional)

    78	        Restrict the automation to a specific lock or set of locks.
    79	        When empty, the actions run for any lock the event entity
    80	        reports. When one or more locks are selected, the actions
    81	        only run when one of those locks is the lock the credential

    83	      default: []
    84	      selector:
    85	        entity:
    86	          domain: lock
    87	          multiple: true
    88	    notify_actions:
    89	      name: Actions
    90	      description: >
    91	        The actions to run when a credential is used. You can configure
    92	        any HA action here — notifications, scripts, etc. Use
    93	        template variables like `{{ slot_name }}` and
    94	        `{{ lock_name }}` in your action data.
    95	      selector:
    96	        action:
    97	
    98	mode: queued
    99	max: 10
   100	
   101	triggers:
   102	  - trigger: state
   103	    entity_id: !input event_entity
   104	    not_to:
   105	      - unknown
   106	      - unavailable
   107	
   108	variables:
   109	  event_entity_id: !input event_entity
   110	  locks: !input locks
   111	  # Variables are computed before conditions run, so guard every
   112	  # `trigger.to_state` access against the entity-removal case
   113	  # (`to_state is None`) — otherwise the variable rendering errors
   114	  # out before the conditions below can block the action.
   115	
   116	  # `event_type` is the fixed word `credential_used` and names nothing;
   117	  # `target` is what the credential was used against, which is a lock when
   118	  # a lock observed the use and can be anything at all when the
   119	  # `use_credential` action reported one.

   148	  credential_type: >-
   149	    {{ trigger.to_state.attributes.event_type | default('unknown', true)
   150	       if trigger.to_state is not none else 'unknown' }}

   153	  # Block transitions that aren't real PIN uses:

"""
User-name rules for Lock Code Manager slots.

The name is the identity the configuration is keyed on, so it has to be
present and unique within its entry.

This module is the single place those rules live, so the config flow
(validating new input) and the migration (repairing existing data) cannot
drift from each other.
"""

from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from typing import Any

from homeassistant.const import CONF_NAME


def normalize_name(name: str | None) -> str:
    """
    Return ``name`` in the form Lock Code Manager stores and compares.

    Surrounding whitespace is removed so two names that differ only by
    padding cannot both be stored. An identity that can differ invisibly is
    worse than useless -- the user would see two identical rows and Lock
    Code Manager would treat them as distinct users.
    """
    return (name or "").strip()


def identity(name: str | None) -> str:
    """
    Return the form a user is recognized by.

    Whitespace normalized and casefolded, so ``Bob`` and ``BOB `` are one
    person everywhere. Comparing any other way lets the same user hold two
    credential indices, and makes a case-only rename read as a deletion plus
    an addition.
    """
    return normalize_name(name).casefold()


def name_error(name: str | None) -> str | None:
    """
    Return the validation error key for ``name``, or ``None`` when valid.

    Returns a translation key rather than a message so callers can surface
    it in the user's language.
    """
    if not normalize_name(name):
        return "name_required"
    return None


def fallback_name(slot_num: int) -> str:
    """Return the name given to a slot that has none."""
    return f"User {slot_num}"


def deduplicate(name: str, taken: Iterable[str]) -> str:
    """
    Return ``name``, suffixed if needed so it does not collide with ``taken``.

    Suffixes with " 2", " 3", and so on. Comparison is case-insensitive
    because two users differing only in case would be indistinguishable in
    the frontend and would collide once slugified into an entity identifier.
    """
    lowered = {identity(existing) for existing in taken}
    if identity(name) not in lowered:
        return name
    suffix = 2
    while identity(f"{name} {suffix}") in lowered:
        suffix += 1
    return f"{name} {suffix}"

## Displaying Condition Helper Controls Inline

When using helper entities (such as `input_datetime`, `input_number`, or `input_boolean`) alongside condition entities, you can display those helper controls directly within the LCM user card using the `condition_helpers` configuration property. This lets you adjust condition parameters (for example, start/end dates for a date range condition) without navigating away from the LCM dashboard.

### Configuration

The `condition_helpers` property accepts a list of helper entity IDs to display inline for a given user. It can be set at three levels. At the dashboard and view levels the map is keyed by the user's internal slot number (see [[Finding a slot number|Blueprints#finding-a-slot-number]]); at the card level it is a plain list, since the card already identifies the user:

**Dashboard level** — applies across all views and cards:

```yaml
strategy:
  type: custom:lock-code-manager
  condition_helpers:
    config_entry_id_here:
      1:
        - input_datetime.guest_start
        - input_datetime.guest_end
```

**View level** — applies to all cards in the view:

```yaml
strategy:
  type: custom:lock-code-manager
  config_entry_id: abc123
  condition_helpers:
    1:
      - input_datetime.guest_start
      - input_datetime.guest_end
```

**Card level** — applies to a single user card:

```yaml
type: custom:lcm-user
config_entry_id: abc123
name: Guest
condition_helpers:
  - input_datetime.guest_start
  - input_datetime.guest_end
```

### Example: Date Range with Inline Controls

1. Create `input_datetime.guest_start` and `input_datetime.guest_end` helpers.
2. Use the [[Date Range Condition blueprint|Blueprints#date-range-condition]] to create a binary sensor from those helpers.
3. Assign the binary sensor as the condition entity for the user.
4. Add `condition_helpers` to your dashboard configuration so the start/end dates can be adjusted directly from the user card.
